newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends down on BOJ Fukui rate remark.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends down on BOJ Fukui rate remark.

text.p: Key December three-month Euroyen futures fell sharply after Bank of Japan (BOJ) deputy governor Toshihiko Fukui was quoted as saying that the BOJ is mulling the right timing to raise the official discount rate.

"Fukui's remark on the rate threw a massive amount of cold water on the market and drowned some traders. The (Fukui's) message was very strong and so 'un-BOJish'," said a city bank trader. December fell to as low as 98.86 in late trading.

Fukui also said that the BOJ does not want to make a hasty decision on monetary policy. The remarks were made at a meeting with business executives of Japan's largest grouping of labour unions, at which the group urged the BOJ to raise the rate.
December moved in a range of 98.86-98.99.

In early trade, December was firmer on weak Tokyo stocks and the strong yen. The main factor behind weaker stocks was selling of futures by foreign investors, who see a chance that Japan's exporters may revise down their earnings forecasts in view of the dollar's steep fall, which in turn could delay a credit tightening, money traders said.
Fukui's remark crushed traders' hopes that the yen's steep rise might delay the timing of a credit tightening.

Fukui, also said that the April 1 rise in Japan's consumption tax to five percent from three percent may have a gradual impact on consumption and that the economic activities of small and medium-sized companies were not yet robust enough.
But, these cautious lines on the economy were ignored by the market which was depressed by his earlier comments.
Later, a BOJ spokesman said that the central bank will continue to carry out its monetary policy of putting emphasis on strengthening the basis for economic recovery.
